text:
Adam Fantilli told The Columbus Dispatch he was "not nervous at all" about his slow start, and there is a case for calm. He has seven points in 18 games while playing 20:46 a night, and only two assists. His points per 60 sit at 1.12, roughly half his rate from last season.

The shooting part looks fine. He has 52 shots and five goals on 5.54 expected (expected goals measure chance quality), close to even. What has dried up is everything around him: the Blue Jackets get 47% of the expected goals with him at five on five, below their rate without him, and he has been on the ice for fewer chances than we would expect from him over the last ten games. That has cost him assists.

The defensive question from last season is still open. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice than with all but 6% of forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile for chances from in front of the net, so the scoring instinct is real. He has one goal in his last eight games. Columbus needs the assists to return.
headline: Fantilli's slow start, by the numbers
